title: Equivariant semistable modification of a marked nodal tower
statement: A trait means the spectrum of a discrete valuation ring, a Noetherian local domain of dimension one with principal maximal ideal. A complete strictly henselian trait has a maximal-ideal-adically complete henselian coordinate ring with separably closed residue field. Mixed characteristic means fraction-field characteristic zero and positive residue characteristic. Let $T$ be a complete strictly henselian mixed-characteristic trait and $Y_d\to\cdots\to Y_0=T$ a marked split nodal tower of length $d\ge1$. Let a finite group $G$ act equivariantly on this tower (including possibly nontrivially on $T$) with the splitting property on fibre dual graphs described below. Then there exist an integral regular scheme $Z$, projective over $T$, and a $G$-equivariant projective birational morphism $h:Z\to Y_d$. Here birational means that $h$ restricts to an isomorphism over a dense open of $Y_d$. The map $Z\to T$ is strictly semistable: etale locally $Z$ has an etale $T$-morphism to $\operatorname{Spec}A[t_1,\ldots,t_n]/(t_1\cdots t_r-\pi)$ with $1\le r\le n$, where $T=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $\pi$ is a uniformizer. The reduced inverse image of $B_d$ is a strict normal crossings divisor [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary] (its distinct irreducible components are regular, all their scheme-theoretic intersections are regular of the expected codimensions, and locally its equation is a product of distinct regular parameters). A marked split nodal tower over a trait $T$ is a tower $Y_d\xrightarrow{f_d}\cdots\xrightarrow{f_1}Y_0=T$ of integral schemes, each $f_i$ projective and flat of finite presentation with geometrically connected reduced fibres of pure dimension one whose only singularities are ordinary double points (completed geometric local ring $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$). Write $B_0=T_s$ for the closed point. Each $f_i$ has finitely many disjoint sections $\sigma_{ij}$ in its relative smooth locus; set $B_i=f_i^{-1}(B_{i-1})\cup\bigcup_j\sigma_{ij}(Y_{i-1})$ as a closed set. The map $f_i$ is smooth outside $B_{i-1}$. Split means that each fibre's irreducible components are smooth and geometrically irreducible over the residue field of its base point and each of its nodes and its two branches are rational over the residue field of the base point. For a group action, the tower is equivariant, the unions of sections are stable, and the stabilizer of a base point acts trivially on the dual graph of its fibre. The dual graph has one vertex for each geometric irreducible component, one edge with its two ends for each node, and an attached marked leg for each section. Integral, regular, flat, finite type, finite, projective, and etale use [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-weil-regular-scheme], [def-weil-flat-morphism], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], [def-kun-projective], and [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Normal means all local rings are integrally closed domains. Quasi-projective means admitting a locally closed immersion into some finite-dimensional projective space over the base. Smoothness is as in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and geometric integrality, reducedness, connectedness and irreducibility as in [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible].

source.place: Expose X Lemma 2.5, proof, successive applications of Vidal 2004b Proposition 4.4.4 and its following remark, p.153 (regular equivariant modifications and strictly semistable total space). This is the nodal-tower modification input, before the quotient/Sylow steps. Vidal primary article WANTED locally.

proof.text: Write $T=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and choose a uniformizer $\pi$. The ring $A$ is excellent by [lem-per-complete-local-excellence]. We induct on $i$ from $0$ to $d$. Our invariant is a $G$-equivariant projective birational $h_i:Z_i\to Y_i$ with $Z_i$ integral regular and projective over $T$, and $G$-strict strict normal crossings boundary $E_i=(h_i^{-1}B_i)_{\mathrm{red}}$. Here $G$-strict means that distinct translates of any one irreducible component are disjoint. Etale locally over the closed fibre there are compatible $T$-charts etale over $\operatorname{Spec}A[t_1,\ldots,t_n]/(t_1\cdots t_r-\pi)$ with $E_i$ defined by $t_1\cdots t_m=0$, $1\le r\le m\le n$. Over the generic fibre the analogous charts are smooth coordinate charts with a coordinate-hyperplane boundary. Point stabilizers fix all geometric local branches of $E_i$. For $i=0$ take $Z_0=T$, $h_0=1$, $E_0=T_s$: the chart $A[t_1]/(t_1-\pi)=A$ proves the closed-fibre assertions; the generic fibre has empty boundary. The closed point and its single branch are fixed by every automorphism of $T$.

source.place: Expose X Lemma 2.5, proof, printed p.153: successive applications of Vidal 2004b Proposition 4.4.4 and its following remark.

proof.text: Assume the invariant for $i-1$, and form $C_i=Y_i\times_{Y_{i-1}}Z_{i-1}$ with maps $p_i:C_i\to Y_i$ and $F_i:C_i\to Z_{i-1}$. Projectivity of $F_i$ and $p_i$ follows from [lem-pc-projective-base-change]. The latter is a base change of $h_{i-1}$. Flatness and finite presentation of $F_i$ follow directly by tensoring: for an affine presentation $B=R[x_1,\ldots,x_a]/(q_1,\ldots,q_b)$ its pullback is $R'[x_1,\ldots,x_a]/(q_1,\ldots,q_b)$; tensoring an injection of $R'$-modules with $B\otimes_RR'$ is tensoring its underlying $R$-module injection with the flat $R$-algebra $B$. The fibre at a geometric point of $Z_{i-1}$ is the corresponding original geometric fibre of $f_i$. Thus the nodal, reduced, connected, dimension-one and split graph assertions, including smoothness of each fibre component after field extension, persist. Pull back the sections, calling their union $D_i$. They remain disjoint. Smoothness is preserved here directly from [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]: a first-order lifting problem on the pullback projects to one for $f_i$, whose lift pairs with the fixed map to $Z_{i-1}$. The displayed finite presentations supply the other part of that definition. Hence $D_i$ stays in the relative smooth locus and $F_i$ is smooth off $E_{i-1}$.

source.place: Expose X Lemma 2.5, proof, printed p.153: successive applications of Vidal 2004b Proposition 4.4.4 and its following remark.

proof.text: The scheme $C_i$ is integral. Indeed $h_{i-1}$ identifies the function fields of its integral source and target. The generic fibre of $F_i$ is therefore the original generic fibre of $Y_i/Y_{i-1}$, which is integral (on affines it is localization of a domain). A flat local algebra over a domain injects into its localization at the nonzero base elements: tensor the injection of the base into its fraction field with that flat algebra. Every local ring of $C_i$ therefore embeds into its generic-fibre localization, which is a domain, and every nonempty open meets that generic fibre. Since the generic fibre is irreducible, it is dense irreducible in $C_i$; the injections also prove reducedness. Let $V\subset Y_{i-1}$ be a dense open where $h_{i-1}$ is an isomorphism. The morphism $f_i$ is dominant: its integral source has nonempty fibres over the integral base by hypothesis. Thus $f_i^{-1}V$ is dense open in $Y_i$, and $p_i$ is an isomorphism there. This proves birationality of $p_i$. All pullback actions and sections are equivariant. The stabilizer of a point of $Z_{i-1}$ is a subgroup of that of its image in $Y_{i-1}$; its action on the unchanged split fibre graph is consequently trivial.

source.place: Expose X Lemma 2.5, proof, printed p.153: successive applications of Vidal 2004b Proposition 4.4.4 and its following remark.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-split-nodal-relative-resolution-charts] to $F_i:C_i\to Z_{i-1}$ and $E_{i-1},D_i$. Its integral-source and split-fibre hypotheses are Steps 2--3, and the $G$-strict strict boundary condition on the regular base is the induction invariant. The ambient excellent affine base is $\operatorname{Spec}A$ from Step 1. Projectivity of $Z_{i-1}/T$ makes it quasi-projective and finite type, the latter by [lem-kun-projective-implies-proper] and [def-weil-proper-morphism]; it is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. This verifies every ambient finiteness hypothesis of the one-curve lemma. Write its output as $r_i:Z_i\to C_i$ and put $h_i=p_ir_i$. The lemma gives integral regular $Z_i$, a projective birational equivariant $r_i$, its two local relative charts, and a $G$-strict strict normal crossings reduced inverse boundary. The new reduced boundary is precisely $h_i^{-1}B_i$: indeed $F_i^{-1}E_{i-1}=p_i^{-1}f_i^{-1}B_{i-1}$ as closed sets, and $D_i$ is the pullback of the original union of sections. Apply $r_i^{-1}$ and use the recursive definition of $B_i$.

source.place: Expose X Lemma 2.5, proof, printed p.153: successive applications of Vidal 2004b Proposition 4.4.4 and its following remark.

proof.text: Check the adapted semistable chart invariant from the two relative charts in Step 4. In a smooth chart simply adjoin its relative coordinate $w$ to the previous $T$-chart; the boundary gains $w=0$ only at a marking. In a nodal chart replace one boundary parameter $t_j$ by $uv$. If $j\le r$, eliminate $t_j$ from the two equations $t_1\cdots t_r=\pi$ and $uv=t_j$. The resulting equation is $(\prod_{k\le r,\ k\ne j}t_k)uv=\pi$, a product of distinct variables. If $r<j\le m$, eliminating $t_j$ leaves $t_1\cdots t_r=\pi$ unchanged, with $u,v$ now additional horizontal parameters. In either case the reduced boundary is the product of those distinct parameters obtained from $t_1\cdots t_m$ by the same substitution. Over the generic fibre only the horizontal case occurs and the models are smooth affine-coordinate models. These are etale charts over the indicated $T$-models: the map from the $Y$-relative model to the substituted $T$-model is the base change of the previous etale chart; compose it with the etale map furnished in Step 4. The base-change and composition assertions for etale maps are the scheme case of [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence]. Thus no repeated factor of $\pi$ is introduced. This proves the semistable and boundary chart assertions needed in the induction.

source.place: Expose X Lemma 2.5, proof, printed p.153: successive applications of Vidal 2004b Proposition 4.4.4 and its following remark.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-h-projective-composition], $h_i=p_ir_i$ is projective, and $Z_i\to C_i\to Z_{i-1}\to T$ is projective. The composite $h_i$ is birational in the dense-open convention: take a dense isomorphism open for $p_i$, restrict a dense isomorphism open for $r_i$ to its inverse image, and transport it across the first isomorphism. Both sources are integral, so the intersections are nonempty dense. Equivariance is preserved under composition. Steps 4--5 give the remaining inductive assertions, including the $G$-strict strict boundary for the next stage. The induction now reaches $d$. Set $Z=Z_d$ and $h=h_d$. Regularity, integrality, projectivity and birational equivariance have just been proved; Step 5 gives exactly the strict semistable charts required in the item. The one-curve lemma in Step 4 gives the global strict normal crossings assertion for $E_d=(h^{-1}B_d)_{\mathrm{red}}$ as well as the local boundary charts of Step 5. Thus the conclusion is strict normal crossings, including regularity of each global boundary component.

It is named in the report with a counterexample, and it matches what ILO X 2.5 claims (H1-equivariant strict snc divisor, strict semistable pair), which is what the induction needs. Counterexample checked: y^2z=x^3+x^2z+pi z^3 has a regular total space (f = -pi mod m^2), and its self-nodal special fibre cannot be made strict snc by point blowups (Stacks 0C5R). My own d=2 conifold test, xy=uv=pi, shows the weak split hypothesis fails for this route. Steps checked: S1 complete local ring is excellent, invariant stated with base case; S2 projective base change, flat/fp via tensor, smooth via lifting, fibres keep split smooth components; S3 flat over an integral base with integral generic fibre gives integral C_i, p_i birational; S4 every hypothesis of the new node checked, and the boundary identity follows from the recursive B_i; S5 j<=r gives (prod t_k)uv=pi, j>r is horizontal, etale by base change and composition; S6 projective composition and dense-open birationality. New node: B1-B7 OK; small cases checked (E empty, uv=t, uv=t^2, uv=t1t2, G-strictness excludes swapped branches); not a duplicate of lem-trf-nodal-pair-projective-resolution (field, no group), lem-trf-log-regular-desingularization, lem-trf-normal-crossings-strictification or lem-per-log-regular-projective-log-resolution; not a clause of the parent. lean.statement: theorem exists_markedNodalTower_semistableModification (R : CommRingCat.{u}) [IsDomain R] [IsDiscreteValuationRing R] [IsAdicComplete (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) R] [IsStrictlyHenselianLocalRing R] [CharZero (FractionRing R)] (hchar : ∃ p : ℕ, p.Prime ∧ CharP (IsLocalRing.ResidueField R) p) (G : Type v) [Group G] [Finite G] (d : ℕ) (hd : 1 ≤ d) (N : MarkedSplitNodalTower (Spec R) {IsLocalRing.closedPoint R} G d) : ∃ (Z : Scheme.{u}) (h : Z ⟶ N.Y (Fin.last d)) (ρ : G →* Aut Z), IsIntegral Z ∧ IsRegularScheme Z ∧ IsHProjective h ∧ IsHProjective (h ≫ N.toBase (Fin.last d)) ∧ (∀ g : G, (ρ g).hom ≫ h = h ≫ (N.action (Fin.last d) g).hom) ∧ (∃ U : (N.Y (Fin.last d)).Opens, Dense (U : Set (N.Y (Fin.last d))) ∧ IsIso (h ∣_ U)) ∧ (∃ π : R, Irreducible π ∧ ∀ z : Z, ∃ (n r : ℕ) (_ : 1 ≤ r) (_ : r ≤ n) (V : Z.Etale) (c : V.left ⟶ Spec (.of (monomialTraitAlgebra R π n (fun i ↦ if i.val < r then 1 else 0)))), z ∈ Set.range V.hom ∧ Etale c ∧ c ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (monomialTraitAlgebraMap R π n (fun i ↦ if i.val < r then 1 else 0))) = V.hom ≫ h ≫ N.toBase (Fin.last d)) ∧ ∃ E : Z.IdealSheafData, IsStrictNormalCrossingsBoundary E ∧ (E.support : Set Z) = h ⁻¹' (N.boundary (Fin.last d) : Set (N.Y (Fin.last d)))
